_comment: Soil presets. Values are screening estimates from earthmoving handbooks and NRCS soil-series descriptions, not site measurements; replace with test-pit data for a real site. cutting_kpa is specific cutting energy (kPa = kJ per bank m3) for a small blade or box scraper; cone_index_kpa feeds the Brixius tyre model.

ne_glacial_till.label: New England glacial till (rocky clay loam, dense basal till), dry season
ne_glacial_till.notes: Cobbles and boulders make up 10-30 % of till by volume; a refusal is a stone the blade cannot pass that has to be dug out by hand or a bar. Dense basal till (hardpan) at 0.5-1 m cuts far harder than the topsoil above it.
ne_glacial_till._conventional: Hard digging in dense, stony till: partial buckets and slow cycles

ne_glacial_till_wet.label: New England glacial till, wet spring (perched water table, saturated clay)
ne_glacial_till_wet.notes: Wet clay cuts more easily but is sticky (loose_cut_factor up) and tyres lose most of their grip. A perched water table sits on the dense till in spring.
ne_glacial_till_wet._conventional: Easier to dig, sticky to dump; wheeled loaders rut and slow badly on saturated clay

florida_sand.label: Florida fine sand (sandy lot, shallow water table)
florida_sand.notes: Easy to cut, no rock, but loose sand gives poor grip and high rolling resistance, and below the water table the trench floor is saturated. Sand banks need flatter slopes (1V:2H).
florida_sand._conventional: Full buckets and fast cycles; loose sand slows wheeled carry
